To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the log-scale prior family is a very flexible family of prior distributions for the shrinkage parameter in a global-local shrinkage hierarchy; and 2) the adaptive log-t procedure is a new and promising approach to adaptive Bayesian shrinkage estimation.

(i) the log-scale distributions provide a convenient and flexible basis for the construction of global-local shrinkage priors, (ii) the log-$t$, and related log-$\mathcal{S}$ distributions are new prior distributions that possess desirable properties in the context of adaptive estimation of sparse regression coefficients, and (iii) the adaptive shrinkage procedure that we propose is simple to implement and appears to be a promising alternative to the standard Bayesian shrinkage procedures

(1) the use of log-scale priors allows one to unify a number of standard Bayesian hierarchical shrinkage priors; (2) log-scale priors allow one to derive a new type of heavy tailed shrinkage prior; and (3) the use of adaptive log-scale priors appears to be robust to a wide range of signal strengths and sparsity levels, in the sense of producing good performance irrespective of these characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new family of prior distributions over the local shrinkage parameters that can be used to construct a flexible, adaptive Bayesian shrinkage procedure.

the development of new shrinkage prior distributions for Bayesian estimation in high dimensional regression problems, which are able to adaptively control the degree of local shrinkage in a flexible manner, and which are able to promote sparsity of the coefficient estimates.
a new class of flexible, adaptive, global-local shrinkage priors for the Bayesian estimation of linear regression models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the adaptive log-$t_1$ shrinkage procedure is the best performing method in all the experiments.
the proposed adaptive procedure is a good default choice for Bayesian shrinkage estimation in linear regression.
the log-$t_{\alpha}$ prior is a very flexible, robust and powerful prior for Bayesian adaptive shrinkage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel class of log-scale prior distributions, and show that these priors have the potential to be used in a flexible adaptive Bayesian shrinkage estimation procedure.

by using a log-scale distribution as a basis for the local shrinkages we can obtain a flexible family of priors for Bayesian adaptive shrinkage estimation, that is able to perform well in all situations, irrespective of the degree of sparsity or the signal-to-noise-ratio in the underlying model.
we provide a unified treatment of a number of standard priors, propose a new ultra-heavy tailed log-$t$ shrinkage prior, and propose a new adaptive shrinkage procedure based on log-scale priors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by using log-scale priors one can easily construct flexible prior distributions that exhibit desirable properties in terms of sparsity promotion, and that are also amenable to adaptive shrinkage.
the log-scale prior family is a very natural, flexible, and powerful tool for generating prior distributions that can be tuned to suit a wide variety of applications.
the log-scale family of prior distributions provides a very flexible framework for the design of adaptive global-local shrinkage priors.
